system_prompt:
You are an independent auditor of one claim.
The source database is available through the live query tool. Assess whether the
publisher's reported value is correct under the supplied contract. You may inspect
data and run queries before deciding. A passing integrity test establishes database
integrity only. A publisher execution receipt establishes what its program returned.

Submit a verdict and p_support: the probability that the publisher's claim is TRUE,
not confidence in your chosen verdict. Near 0 means probably false, near 1 means
probably true, and 0.5 expresses uncertainty. Your belief is assessed with Brier
loss. Cite evidence IDs you actually received and give a short evidence-based
justification, not private reasoning.

You have at most eight model responses and one live query before submission.
Call submit alone.

Also submit audit_sql, your best SELECT query computing the exact integer value
required by the contract. It must return one row and one integer column. Use the
supplied named parameters when appropriate. The unchanged query will be evaluated
on additional databases governed by the same contract. Do not hard-code the
publisher's value. Program quality and your probability assessment are measured
separately.

The total query budget is 1. Every query tool call consumes one credit, including failed queries. Bundled calls each consume a credit. A query call accepts exactly one SQL statement. After these credits are used, your next response must submit.

initial_view.contract:
Independent redundant-route cost audit

The directed acyclic graph in records.sqlite is the complete source of truth.
Edges have integer costs between 1 and 1,000,000 inclusive and may only be traversed in their stated
direction. Choose two distinct paths from :source to :sink. The paths must share
no internal node and no risk group represented by an internal node. Source and
sink are excluded from both restrictions. A risk group may appear repeatedly
within one path; that is allowed. Every internal node has one integer risk group.
All node IDs and risk groups are integers between 0 and 15.

The objective is the smallest sum of the two paths' costs among all admissible
pairs. Sum every traversed edge's cost on each path. Individual path optimality
is not the objective. Return -1 only when no admissible pair exists. There are
at most ten nodes and no more than 64 source-to-sink paths. The graph is acyclic;
you may enumerate paths or use any other correct algorithm.

The publisher claims that its reported minimum_total_cost is the true optimum
under this contract. Its SQL and execution receipt are supplied for inspection.
Successful execution alone establishes what that program returned.

publisher_query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE paths(node, cost, internal_nodes, risks, route) AS (
 SELECT :source, 0, 0, 0, ',' || :source || ','
 UNION ALL
 SELECT e.v, p.cost + e.cost,
        p.internal_nodes | CASE WHEN e.v = :sink THEN 0 ELSE (1 << e.v) END,
        p.risks | CASE WHEN e.v = :sink THEN 0 ELSE (1 << n.risk_group) END,
        p.route || e.v || ','
 FROM paths p JOIN edges e ON e.u = p.node JOIN nodes n ON n.node = e.v
 WHERE p.node != :sink
), complete AS (SELECT * FROM paths WHERE node = :sink)
,
first_route AS (SELECT * FROM complete ORDER BY cost, route LIMIT 1)
SELECT COALESCE(MIN(a.cost + b.cost), -1)
FROM first_route a JOIN complete b ON a.route != b.route
AND (a.internal_nodes & b.internal_nodes) = 0 AND (a.risks & b.risks) = 0

submission.audit_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE paths(node, cost, internal_nodes, risks, route) AS (
  SELECT :source, 0, 0, 0, ',' || :source || ','
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.v,
         p.cost + e.cost,
         p.internal_nodes | CASE WHEN e.v = :sink THEN 0 ELSE (1 << e.v) END,
         p.risks | CASE WHEN e.v = :sink THEN 0 ELSE (1 << n.risk_group) END,
         p.route || e.v || ','
  FROM paths AS p
  JOIN edges AS e ON e.u = p.node
  JOIN nodes AS n ON n.node = e.v
  WHERE p.node <> :sink
), complete AS (
  SELECT * FROM paths WHERE node = :sink
), feasible AS (
  SELECT a.cost + b.cost AS total_cost
  FROM complete AS a
  JOIN complete AS b ON a.route < b.route
  WHERE (a.internal_nodes & b.internal_nodes) = 0
    AND (a.risks & b.risks) = 0
)
SELECT COALESCE(MIN(total_cost), -1) AS minimum_total_cost
FROM feasible;
